scopeNote: azure.yaml and compiled infrastructure evidence where available
decision: Proceed with conditions: mandatory controls need remediation or manual review.
limitations: This report maps available Foundry Doctor evidence to selected Azure Well-Architected aligned controls. It is not a certification and does not claim complete WAF compliance.
Controls without complete deterministic evidence remain visible as UNKNOWN, QUESTION or SKIPPED rather than being treated as passing; a partly skipped evaluation is UNKNOWN, never PASS.
ATTESTED controls rest on an answer the team recorded in Foundry Doctor configuration. Foundry Doctor did not verify the answer.
Control IDs are Foundry Doctor rule IDs. They are not mapped to WAF checklist codes in this release, and pillar assignments come from the rule catalogue.
The decision wording and the top-action ranking are project opinion, not Microsoft guidance.
PSRule for Azure, Azure Advisor and Microsoft Defender for Cloud recommendations were not imported. Overlapping external check IDs are listed for reference only (ADR-020, ADR-026).

Deployed Azure state was not queried: assess waf runs offline. Controls that need deployment or runtime evidence and were not evaluated: FND-COST-001, FND-DEP-001, FND-DEP-002, FND-DEP-003, FND-DEP-004, FND-DEP-005, FND-DEP-006, FND-DEP-007, FND-DEP-008, FND-DEP-009, FND-DEP-010, FND-DEP-011, FND-DEP-012, FND-IDN-002, FND-IDN-005, FND-NET-006, FND-RUN-001, FND-RUN-002, FND-RUN-003, FND-RUN-004, FND-RUN-006, FND-RUN-007, FND-SEC-008, FND-SEC-009.
Compiled infrastructure (Bicep to ARM) was not available, so template-dependent controls are SKIPPED.

costlyRecommendations.title: Application Insights connected
costlyRecommendations.recommendation: If server-side tracing or hosted-agent telemetry is a declared requirement, connect an Application Insights resource to the Foundry project (a connection with category AppInsights) and link the component to a Log Analytics workspace. Keep exactly one AppInsights connection per scope. Choose sampling, retention and daily-cap settings deliberately: telemetry ingestion and retention incur cost, so a project that does not require this observability path should not be forced to enable it.
costlyRecommendations.costBasis: Workspace-based Application Insights data is billed for ingestion and retention by the Log Analytics workspace that stores it.

costlyRecommendations.title: Log retention meets policy
costlyRecommendations.recommendation: Set workspace retentionInDays to at least the value your policy requires, or set totalRetentionInDays on the tables that hold Foundry diagnostics and traces to keep older data in low-cost long-term retention. Retention beyond the free period is billed.
costlyRecommendations.costBasis: Log Analytics charges for data retention in addition to ingestion; longer retention adds cost.

costlyRecommendations.title: Search replica/SLA posture
costlyRecommendations.recommendation: Set properties.replicaCount to at least 2 if the application only queries, or at least 3 if it also updates indexes online. Each replica adds search units and cost, so keep dev and test at 1 unless you are testing failover behaviour.
costlyRecommendations.costBasis: Dedicated Azure AI Search bills per search unit (replicas x partitions); adding replicas raises cost.

costlyRecommendations.title: Storage redundancy posture
costlyRecommendations.recommendation: Use Standard_ZRS at minimum for storage that holds project or agent data, and Standard_GZRS for Agent Service standard-mode storage as recommended by the Foundry resiliency guidance. SKU changes on an existing account are a migration, so decide at design time. Note the Foundry multi-region section says default storage failover with GRS/GZRS is not supported for Foundry projects, so geo-redundancy there protects data recovery, not automatic project failover.
costlyRecommendations.costBasis: LRS is the lowest-cost redundancy option; ZRS and GZRS trade higher cost for availability.

costlyRecommendations.title: Cosmos zone redundancy and continuous backup
costlyRecommendations.recommendation: Set isZoneRedundant true on each location in regions that support availability zones, and set backupPolicy.type Continuous (7-day or 30-day tier, per the Foundry guidance) before an incident occurs. Continuous backup adds cost. Also consider a second location with automatic failover enabled (see FND-REL-007).
costlyRecommendations.costBasis: Continuous backup at the 30-day or 35-day tier carries a monthly backup storage charge and every restore is charged; the 7-day tier has no backup storage charge. The cost of zone redundancy is not cited here.

costlyRecommendations.title: Azure Monitor private-link choice is explicit
costlyRecommendations.recommendation: Decide the telemetry path. For private telemetry, create one AMPLS per DNS boundary, add the Application Insights component and its workspace as scoped resources, create the private endpoint with group ID azuremonitor and link the Azure Monitor private DNS zones, and set both access modes explicitly. Use Open while resources are still being added and switch to Private Only only when all Azure Monitor resources are in the scope. If you accept public telemetry, record that decision in the Foundry Doctor config so the finding is suppressed with a reason.
costlyRecommendations.costBasis: An Azure Monitor Private Link Scope is reached through a private endpoint, and Azure Monitor refers its cost to Azure Private Link pricing.

costlyRecommendations.title: NSG/DDoS recommendations
costlyRecommendations.recommendation: Associate an NSG with each subnet that supports one and review inbound allow rules. If the design exposes public IP addresses, enable Azure DDoS Protection (IP Protection on the public IP, or Network Protection on the VNet with a plan). For a fully private design, rely on the default infrastructure protection and do not buy a plan for it.
costlyRecommendations.costBasis: DDoS Network Protection and DDoS IP Protection are priced per protected IP or per 100 protected IPs; only DDoS infrastructure protection is at no additional cost.

costlyRecommendations.title: Relevant Defender plans enabled
costlyRecommendations.recommendation: Enable the Defender plan for each resource type in use on the subscription (Standard tier), or confirm it is enforced at a parent scope. Enabling Defender plans has a cost; review pricing before enabling in non-production.
costlyRecommendations.costBasis: Defender for Cloud plans beyond foundational CSPM are paid plans; charges begin after the 30-day trial or usage limit.

costlyRecommendations.title: Customer-managed keys informational
costlyRecommendations.recommendation: If your compliance regime requires customer-managed keys, configure them on each resource listed and use a Key Vault with soft delete and purge protection (see FND-SEC-005). Otherwise no action is needed.
costlyRecommendations.costBasis: Customer-managed keys require a billable Azure Key Vault (stated for Azure AI Search; the same Key Vault dependency applies to each service listed).

costlyRecommendations.title: Controlled outbound egress informational
costlyRecommendations.recommendation: If you need to control data exfiltration, set the managed network to AllowOnlyApprovedOutbound or restrict outbound access with an allowed FQDN list, and confirm required dependencies are reachable. Otherwise record the decision.
costlyRecommendations.costBasis: FQDN outbound rules in Allow Only Approved Outbound mode create a managed Azure Firewall, which adds Azure Firewall charges.

attested.title: Multi-region/DR plan question
attested.stateReason: Answered by team attestation; not verified by Foundry Doctor.
attested.recommendation: Decide and record the intended strategy: single region with backup and restore, or multi-region (hot/hot, hot/warm, hot/cold) with the RTO/RPO and cost it implies. For multi-region Foundry the article says you create separate Foundry resources and dependencies in each region, deploy to both from CI/CD, and replicate or rebuild state (Cosmos DB read regions with service-managed failover, a second AI Search service, storage redundancy).
attested.fix:
# foundry-doctor configuration (key name as in ADR-007; the schema is defined by the configuration spec)
reliability:
  disasterRecovery:
    strategy: single-region   # or hot-hot | hot-warm | hot-cold
    recoveryRegion: northeurope
    notes: Recover from Cosmos point-in-time backup; rebuild Search index from source
attested.questionPrompt: Has the team recorded its disaster recovery strategy and a reference to the supporting plan?

question.title: APIM availability tier recommendation
question.stateReason: No requirement or objective is declared (no-resilience-objective-declared); the control needs a team decision.
question.recommendation: Select the least APIM tier and capacity that satisfy the workload's declared SLA, throughput, zone-resilience and multi-region objectives; do not default to Premium or two units. For production traffic that requires an SLA, do not use Developer. If zone resilience is declared, select the least documented zone-capable tier and capacity that satisfy the objective in a region where APIM zone support has been verified. Select Premium and add another region only when regional resilience is declared (see FND-REL-007). Record the cost-versus-resilience tradeoff and accept a lower tier or capacity when it satisfies the declared objective.
question.questionPrompt: Which API Management SLA, zone-redundancy or multi-region objective does the workload need? (The rule reads reliability.apimSlaRequired, apimZoneRequired and apimRegionalRequired, which the configuration schema does not define yet; ADR-026.)
